shots.visual_event: Arin wakes alone in a 1913 wooden carriage; Nila sits opposite, pale clock-light visible in the cracks of her hands.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “They call me Zero so nobody asks who came first.”

shots.visual_event: She shows a living memory: engineer Devika Rao turning a gigantic station clock backward as a derailment approaches.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “My mother stole one minute from death.”

shots.visual_event: Thirteen people step safely away from the crash, but their shadows remain under the wreck; young Nila walks toward the newborn train.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “Someone had to hold the minute open.”

shots.visual_event: Present-day Arin sees rows of passengers frozen behind glass, each wearing a blank ticket.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “The Conductor imprisoned you.” Nila: “The rule did.”

shots.visual_event: The clock-masked Conductor cuts through the memory with his brass ticket punch; Nila’s carriage begins collapsing.
shots.dialogue_audio: Conductor: “She shows truth with the ending removed.”

shots.visual_event: As Arin is pulled out, Nila presses thirteen hairline cracks into his badge.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “Ask him why he still wears a passenger’s coat.”

end_card.text: THE CONDUCTOR WAS ONCE A PASSENGER
